preamble: Loss of glottalization in the glottalized lateral [lˀ] (Americanist l̓, written l' in the practical orthographies). In Upriver Halkomelem (Halq'eméylem) the glottalized resonants lost their glottalization, usually lengthening the preceding vowel, while Island and Downriver Halkomelem keep them (Compton & Gerdts 2005; Wikipedia says glottalized resonants are absent from most Upriver dialects). Island and Downriver qel'q 'wild rose' thus corresponds to Upriver qe:lq. In the Chimakuan languages Powell (1974), as summarized on Wikipedia, reconstructs glottalized resonants that survive in neither Quileute nor Chemakum; *l̓ appears in both as l or ʔl. In Quileute ḳʷáʔl 'three' < *qʷál̓- the resonant is plain and the glottalization remains as a glottal stop before it.

examples.note: Compton & Gerdts (2005), plants page and 'Sounds of Halkomelem'; the shrub name is qel'qulhp vs Upriver qe:lqulhp. The site's consonant chart writes the glottalized resonants m' n' l' y' w', and its sounds page marks a long vowel with a following colon.
Wiktionary lists both as forms of one Halkomelem word.

languageExamples.context: Powell (1974), as summarized on Wikipedia, gives both a plain resonant and a glottal stop + resonant as Quileute reflexes; in these words the glottalization survives as ʔ before the plain resonant
